 Yaxel Lendeborg 
 GSW 
 Forward 
 #1 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Yaxel Lendeborg finished Friday’s loss to the Spurs with three points (1-of-13 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, one assist and one block.
 With Stephen Curry (oblique) unavailable, Lendeborg was going to receive even more defensive attention from the Spurs. Unfortunately for the rookie and those rostering him, Friday’s game was brutal. Lendeborg shot 1-of-11 from inside the arc and checked out for good with 1:58 remaining in the third quarter. Given how well Lendeborg was playing entering Friday, fantasy managers should expect this game to be his low point. The Warriors play four games next week, starting with the Pelicans on Monday.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Steph Curry sustained an oblique abdominal tear and will be re-evaluated in two weeks. 
 Curry sustained the injury in Wednesday’s loss to Houston, and it will keep him out until late November at minimum. In Curry’s absence, De’Anthony Melton should handle an expanded role after logging 25 minutes Wednesday after Curry’s early exit. Will Richard could also see some additional playing time until Curry returns. 
 De'Anthony Melton 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #8 
 De’Anthony Melton finished Wednesday’s loss to the Rockets with 11 points (3-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, one block and three three-pointers. 
 Melton’s final stat line wasn’t much to write home about, but his role may expand for Friday’s game against the Spurs. Stephen Curry left Wednesday’s game with an abdominal injury and is expected to undergo an MRI on Thursday. If Curry misses time, Melton will have a larger role, whether he moves into the starting lineup or continues to come off the bench. 
 Yaxel Lendeborg 
 GSW 
 Forward 
 #1 
 Yaxel Lendeborg amassed 25 points (9-of-19 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), 10 rebounds, two steals and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Rockets. 
 Lendeborg has scored at least 25 points in six games this season. Against the Rockets, he shouldered more of the offensive workload after Stephen Curry (core) exited, finishing with his third double-double. Through 12 games, only Wilt Chamberlain and Rick Barry have scored more points as a rookie in Warriors history than Lendeborg. The Warriors visit the Spurs on Friday in what will be another challenging matchup for Yaxel, especially if Curry can’t play. 
 Stephen Curry 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #30 
 Stephen Curry (abdominals) will not return to Wednesday’s game against the Rockets. 
 Curry appeared to tweak something on his right side during the first quarter and was taken back to the locker room before the period concluded. He’s since been ruled out for the rest of the night with right abdominal soreness. In Curry’s absence, the Warriors will have to rely even more on Yaxel Lendeborg and Brandin Podziemski. 
 Yaxel Lendeborg 
 GSW 
 Forward 
 #1 
 Yaxel Lendeborg produced 23 points (8-of-10 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pelicans. 
 Lendeborg continues to shine for the Warriors, making all four of his three-point attempts on Monday. The rookie forward has scored at least 20 points in six of 11 games and is considered by many to be one of the early favorites for Rookie of the Year. The Warriors play two more games this week, at Houston and San Antonio, so we’ll learn a bit more about Lendeborg in games of that magnitude. 
 Stephen Curry 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #30 
 Stephen Curry tallied 25 points (6-of-10 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), five rebounds, two assists and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pelicans. 
 Curry only played 21 minutes in Monday’s blowout victory, none in the fourth quarter. That’s all the time he needed to notch another career milestone, as the Warriors guard moved past DeMar DeRozan into 16th place on the NBA’s all-time scoring list. Thus far, Curry’s production has exceeded his preseason ADP by a safe distance, as he’s been a top-5 player in nine-cat formats. The Warriors end their week with games against the Rockets and Spurs, two teams that should offer up greater resistance than the Pelicans did. 
 Stephen Curry 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #30 
 Stephen Curry exploded for a game-high 41 points (13-of-19 FGs, 10-of-10 FTs), six rebounds and six assists across 36 minutes to lead the Warriors to a 126-119 overtime win against the Magic on Saturday. 
 Curry’s sublime start to the year continued in this one as he topped the 40-point plateau for the second time in eight games. His signature sequence came in the final minute of regulation when he knocked down a three-pointer before sinking a pair of free throws and converting a go-ahead layup in the closing seconds. He added five points in overtime as Golden State was finally able to pull away for good. The 38-year-old legend has delivered first-round fantasy value so far, averaging 31.3 points through eight games. Are you not entertained? The Warriors are in line for a three-game week that features matchups against the Pelicans, Rockets and Spurs. 
 Yaxel Lendeborg 
 GSW 
 Forward 
 #1 
 Yaxel Lendeborg amassed 23 points (9-of-15 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists and three blocks across 37 minutes in an overtime victory over the Magic on Saturday. 
 Lendeborg continues to be a revelation for Golden State, surpassing the 20-point plateau for the fifth time in 10 games to open his rookie campaign. He and franchise icon Stephen Curry combined for 64 points in a thrilling overtime victory, accounting for more than half of the Warriors’ offensive output. He came through in the clutch, scoring seven of his 23 points in overtime. The 24-year-old rookie sensation should be rostered in all fantasy formats, as he’s quickly establishing himself as a high-volume scoring threat in Golden State’s offense. The Warriors are in line for a three-game week that features matchups against the Pelicans, Rockets and Spurs. 
 Kristaps Porziņģis 
 GSW 
 Forward-Center 
 #7 
 Kristaps Porziņģis announced on his official X.com page that he is stepping away from basketball. 
 Porziņģis’ announcement notes that he is not where he wants to be at this time and is stepping away to focus on his health. Nothing changes from a fantasy perspective, as KP hasn’t played a game this season. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg should continue to see big minutes in the frontcourt. 
 Stephen Curry 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #30 
 Stephen Curry led the Warriors with 29 points (9-of-19 FGs), one rebound, four assists, one steal and six three-pointers in a 120-100 win over the Heat on Thursday. 
 Despite a rough start to this game, Curry got going in the third quarter. After scoring seven points on 2-of-10 shooting in the first half, he scored 14 points in the third quarter alone and eight more points in the fourth to steal the win for Golden State. Curry has been unbelievable to start the season, which has him ranked as one of the best players in fantasy basketball to this point. He’ll look to stay hot against the Magic to wrap up the week on Saturday.

 Isaiah Hartenstein notched 21 points (9-of-10 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 16 rebounds, six assists and one steal in Friday’s loss to the Clippers.
 After scoring no more than seven points in any of Oklahoma City’s first five games in November, Hartenstein has scored at least 20 in two straight games. He was outstanding against the Clippers, shooting 90 percent from the field and providing excellent value in points, rebounds and assists. Providing top-100 fantasy value, Hartenstein is rostered in 84 percent of Yahoo leagues. Given Oklahoma City’s frontcourt injuries, those rostering Hartenstein would be better served holding on to him than entertaining a trade after the last two games. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jared McCain tallied 23 points (8-of-17 FGs), four rebounds, two assists and seven three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Clippers.
 McCain has scored in double figures in four straight games, with Friday’s being the best of the bunch. The Thunder guard shot 7-of-11 from deep against the Clippers, recording season highs in points and three-pointers. McCain will mainly be a “points and triples” option in fantasy leagues, but Oklahoma City’s injuries open the door for him to provide consistent value.

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander finished Friday’s loss to the Clippers with 40 points (15-of-26 FGs, 8-of-11 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
 Gilgeous-Alexander finished with his third 40-point game of the season, but he wishes he’d scored 42 instead of 40. The two-time MVP’s shot as time expired missed the mark, resulting in a 113-112 Clippers victory. After shooting a combined 17-of-42 in two losses to the Trail Blazers, Gilgeous-Alexander was much more efficient on Friday, shooting well over 50 percent from the field. He could be in for another big night to end the week, as the Thunder visit the Kings on Sunday.

 Keaton Wagler produced 14 points (4-of-7 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), two rebounds, one assist and two three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Thunder.
 After reaching double figures in each of his first five games, Wagler totaled 13 points on 4-of-13 shooting in the Clippers’ first two games of November. The rookie has gotten back on track, having scored at least 11 points in four straight games. Wagler remains a deep-league option in redraft formats, while dynasty league managers should be excited for the rookie guard’s future.

 Derrick Jones Jr. accounted for 14 points (5-of-10 FGs), five rebounds, one steal, four blocks and four three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Thunder.
 Thanks mainly to the three-pointers and defensive stats, Jones has been close to a top-100 player in nine-cat formats. Against the Thunder, he shot 4-of-7 from beyond the arc and recorded five “stocks” in 29 minutes. This was Jones’ fourth game this season with at least two three-pointers, one steal and one block. Managers needing help in those categories should consider adding Jones ahead of Sunday’s game against the Hornets.

 Brook Lopez accumulated 26 points (11-of-21 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Thunder.
 After coming off the bench in the Clippers’ first six games, Lopez is approaching the point where he needs to be rostered in 12-team leagues. He’s scored at least 20 points in three of the last four games, with Friday’s total being a season high. Add in the rebounds and three-pointers, and this was a good night for those rostering the veteran center. Isaiah Jackson (5/3/3 with one block), who began the season as the starter, should be rostered only in very deep leagues.

 Darius Garland finished Friday’s win over the Thunder with 24 points (8-of-17 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), four rebounds, seven assists, one block and three three-pointers.
 After being outscored 40-25 in the third quarter, Garland and the Clippers did what needed to be done down the stretch to win the 113-112 thriller. The Clippers’ starting point guard had the game’s biggest shot: a layup through contact and an ensuing free throw with 50.4 seconds left to take the lead for good. Even with the occasional struggles with turnovers, Garland is providing top-100 fantasy value through 11 games.

 Domantas Sabonis put up 21 points (9-of-16 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 12 rebounds, five assists, and a three in the loss on Friday to the Blazers. 
 After a really bad game against the Magic, Sabonis bounced back and went back to his usual self against the Blazers. He looked healthier in this game, which is a good sign. The efficiency has still been good, but it is starting to come down from his super-hot start. He still puts up good counting stats which is why you have Sabonis in the first place. Overall, its been a good season so far.
